subject: ThunderByte throughput spikes & priority adjustment request
messages:
From: Iris Zhang <iris@thunderbyte.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@thunderbyte.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Realtime inference timeouts + unexpected throttling

Hi Aditya,

We're seeing repeated latency spikes and a sharp increase in 429s beginning yesterday evening (UTC). This shows up as:
- P95 latency 2.5x normal for our realtime /chat endpoint
- Large number of 429s between 18:00-19:30 UTC despite staying under our committed tokens/minute according to our client-side metrics
- A small number of 5xx errors that correlate to the throttling windows

I attached a short QoS export that maps our client-side requests to the timestamps where we see throttling (thunderbyte_qos_report.pdf). We rely on consistent low tail latency for our product; this disruption is user-facing and impacting an active rollout.

Can you please escalate? We need:
1) Immediate mitigation to stop the throttling/smoothing to normal throughput
2) Root cause and corrective action (we suspect a rate/burst mismatch)
3) Timeline for permanent fix + audit evidence for configuration changes (SOC2/controls)

Thanks — please loop in whoever is needed.

— Iris
Head of Platform, ThunderByte AI

From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Iris Zhang <iris@thunderbyte.ai>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime inference timeouts + unexpected throttling

Thanks for the details, Iris — and sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating this to our on-call infra/ops and product immediately.

Immediate plan (tentative):
- Dylan: can you confirm whether the 429s are coming from an enforcement policy (quota/burst) vs upstream transient errors?
- If it's policy-related we can apply a temporary per-customer override (short burst increase) while we debug the root cause.
- We'll provide a changelog and compliance artifacts for your audit team.

Iris: can you confirm the most recent window where you still saw errors (timestamp + an example request id if available)? That will help correlate logs.

I'll follow up in 30–60 minutes with an update and a proposed ETA for mitigation.

— Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 17:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime inference timeouts + unexpected throttling

On Thu, Nov 19, 2026 at 4:12 PM Iris Zhang <iris@thunderbyte.ai> wrote:
> We're seeing repeated latency spikes and a sharp increase in 429s beginning yesterday evening (UTC).

Quick triage notes from ops:
- The enforcement logs show the 429s were emitted by our per-customer token-bucket policy for account TB-8921.
- Current configuration: quota = committed tokens/minute, burst window = 10s, burst_capacity = 2x token refill. The customer's client skews requests into short bursts that exhaust the 10s window and trigger throttling.
- This looks like a policy mismatch (client behavior vs. configured burst window) rather than model overload.

Evidence: attached policy_snapshot_20261119.json (policy export) — shows the 10s window value and tokenbucket counters.

Short-term remediation we can do now (pending approvals):
1) Apply a temporary per-account override: increase burst window to 120s and set burst_capacity to 3x for TB-8921.
2) Enable a soft-limit (allow X additional tokens for 10 minutes while we monitor) to avoid abrupt 429 spikes.
3) Monitor for 30–60 minutes; rollback if we observe cross-account impact.

Estimated cost impact: modest (the override increases short-term token consumption risk). We'll capture metrics and send a cost delta estimate to finance if needed.

If you approve, I can push the override within 10–15 minutes and report back.

— Dylan (on-call infra)
From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 18:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime inference timeouts + unexpected throttling

Thanks for the quick triage, Dylan. A couple of product/ops asks before we flip anything wide:
- Can we apply the override as a per-account canary (single cluster/region) rather than a global change? That reduces blast radius.
- Need a clear rollback criterion (e.g., increases in cross-account P99 latency or error rate > threshold).
- Please capture the exact lines for our compliance log (who changed what, timestamp, reason).

If dylan can do a regional canary and provide a 30-min monitoring window, I support the temporary increase. Also we should plan a follow-up to evaluate whether the customer's SDK patterns require guidance or whether the policy should be revised for similar customers.

— Lauren
Product Manager, Inference Platform
From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Iris Zhang <iris@thunderbyte.ai>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@thunderbyte.ai>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Immediate mitigation applied — please validate

Hi Iris / Tom,

Update from ops: we applied a per-account regional override for TB-8921 at 08:18 PT (details below). You should see latency and 429 counts return toward baseline within a few minutes.

What we changed (short-term):
- Burst window increased from 10s -> 120s (regional, per-account override)
- Burst capacity increased from 2x -> 3x for the override period
- Enabled a soft-limit allowance for 10 minutes while we monitor metrics

Monitoring plan: ops will closely monitor P95/P99 latency and cross-account error rates for 60 minutes. We will rollback immediately if we see systemic impact.

Next steps:
1) Can you validate on your side and share 2–3 example request IDs or a small client-side packet showing the previous 429 timestamps?
2) We'll follow up with a permanent configuration proposal and a short mutual action plan (MAP) that includes audit log export for your compliance team.

Apologies again for the interruption — we'll keep this as short as possible.

— Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Iris Zhang <iris@thunderbyte.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@thunderbyte.ai>, support@thunderbyte.ai, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Immediate mitigation applied — please validate

Thanks — confirming we see the improvement. P95 has returned to baseline and 429 spikes dropped by ~95% after ~08:25 PT. Example request id that failed previously: req_20261119_7f3b9e.

A few asks to close the loop:
- Please create the MAP and share the proposed permanent config for TB-8921 (we prefer documented config + an audit entry for SOC2).
- We will need the policy export and timestamped change log for our controls team. A simple XLS with before/after values is fine (proposed_map_TB-8921.xlsx).
- Can you advise whether this is something we should fix client-side (smoothing request pattern) vs you changing platform defaults for similar customers?

Appreciate the rapid response — we'll hold on the rollout for the next 24 hours and validate with our end-to-end tests.

— Iris
Head of Platform, ThunderByte AI
